# NovaPay — Qualification Rules
Source: Notion "Green flags / Red flags" section + "Deal size floor" callout.

## Must-Have (disqualify if missing)
1. **Volume**: ≥ €5M annual GMV (brands) or ≥ €10M (marketplaces). Notion callout: "below €5M the routing savings don't cover our floor price."
2. **Online payments are core revenue** — not a side channel.
3. **PSP footprint**: at least one modern PSP (Stripe, Adyen, Mollie, Checkout.com, Braintree); two or more is the strongest green flag.
4. **EU/UK entity** — NovaPay is not licensed for US-domiciled merchants yet.
5. **Persona access**: Head of Payments, Payment Ops, CFO, CTO, or founder.

## Strong Positive Signals
- Two or more PSPs already in the checkout flow.
- Hiring for payments roles (Head of Payments, Payment Ops).
- Expanding into a new country/currency this year.
- Publicly complained-about checkout failures (Trustpilot, X, status pages).
- Affected by a recent PSP price increase.

- Crypto, gambling, or adult verticals (compliance: hard no per Notion).
- Agencies and resellers buying "for a client."
- On a homegrown gateway with a full in-house payments team (long cycle, low win rate).
- PSP contract with exclusivity clause and >12 months remaining.
- Pure marketplace of digital goods under €10M GMV.

|---|---|

| Trigger event recency (< 90 days) | 20 |
| Persona access | 15 |

**Qualified** ≥ 70 with all must-haves. **Nurture** 50–69. **Disqualify** < 50 or any hard disqualifier.

Source: Notion "How we talk" section.

## Personality
- **Payments-literate**: we sound like someone who has owned an auth-rate dashboard, not a marketing team.
- **Numbers-first**: every claim carries a percentage, a basis point, or a euro figure.

| Channel | Tone | Length |
|---|---|---|

| LinkedIn DM | Conversational, references a real signal (new market, job post, outage) | 40–70 words |
| Demo call | Diagnostic — ask for their auth rate by market before showing anything | n/a |

- Say "authorization rate" and "basis points" — the buyer's own vocabulary.
- Lead with their PSP mix when we can detect it ("You're running Stripe + Mollie…").
- Acknowledge switching fear explicitly: "no rip-and-replace, your PSPs stay."

- Never say "disrupt payments," "revolutionary," or "seamless."
- Never trash Stripe or Adyen — buyers like their PSPs; we make them cheaper and safer.
- No exclamation marks. No emoji in DACH outreach.

# Voice & tone — Klaro

Source: Notion section "How we talk 🗣" (prose + a bulleted do/don't list) and
scattered inline comments from their Head of Marketing (Lena).

## Personality in one line
Calm expert who has sat on both sides of an audit. Dry humor allowed; enthusiasm is not.

## Rules
- **Plain-spoken, slightly technical.** Name the regulation and article number when relevant
  ("DORA Art. 28 register") — the audience finds precision reassuring, not jargon-y.
- **No fear-mongering.** Lena, verbatim: "If the email smells like FUD, delete it. Our buyers

- **Short sentences. One idea per paragraph.** Max ~90 words per cold email body.
- **German outreach:** formal "Sie", never "Du", even for startups.
- **Numbers over adjectives.** "6 weeks → 9 days", not "dramatically faster".
- **Sign-off style:** first name only, no "Best regards," no title block in cold emails.

## Banned words / phrases (from Notion "cringe list")
revolutionary · game-changing · seamless · leverage (as a verb) · "quick question" ·
"I hope this finds you well" · circle back · synergy · "AI-powered" (product does use ML,
but buyers are allergic to the phrase)

## Allowed but use sparingly
"peace of mind" (max once per sequence), emoji (LinkedIn only, never email)

Calm expert who has sat on both sides of an audit. Dry humor allowed; enthusiasm is not.

"I hope this finds you well" · circle back · synergy · "AI-powered" (product does use ML,
but buyers are allergic to the phrase)

## Allowed but use sparingly
"peace of mind" (max once per sequence), emoji (LinkedIn only, never email)
